_publicUrl_comment: The address this instance is reached at from other devices. Clients (the tray app, any future
client) read it from here rather than compiling it in, so nothing in the code is tied to one
host or tailnet. Set it to your own; it is only used to build links, never to bind a socket.
_comment: Journals to watch, by ISSN. Discovery is via the Crossref REST API by ISSN, NOT per-journal RSS:
Crossref is uniform across every publisher, needs no scraping, carries DOI/title/type/date, and does
not break when a publisher changes their feed URL (JAMA's guessed RSS URL already 404s).
tier 1 = practice-changing venue; a stroke RCT here is almost always a must-read.
tier 2 = major specialty journal. tier 3 = worth seeing, lower priority.
Add a journal by appending its print or electronic ISSN - find it on the journal's homepage or at
https://portal.issn.org. Restart the service (or wait for the next ingest) to pick it up.
_topic_comment: A paper is kept if it scores at least minScore. Matching is case-insensitive on title + abstract.
Title matches count double - a stroke paper almost always says so in the title.
Tune these freely; they are the difference between a useful inbox and noise.
_proxy_comment: Library proxy. Most papers in these journals are paywalled, and publishers block automated
download even of their open-access PDFs (verified against Wiley and neurology.org: HTTP 403 to
any non-browser client). So the realistic route to full text is a link through your institution.
mode 'qurl'     uses loginUrl, with %u replaced by the whole target URL, percent-encoded.
mode 'hostname' uses hostPattern, with %h the target host and %p its path and query.
Your library publishes these on its off-campus access page. Editable in the UI under
Library proxy - this file is only the seed for a fresh install.
_ai_comment: Structured summaries through the Claude Code CLI, which runs on an existing Claude
subscription rather than a paid API key. OFF by default: it needs the CLI installed and signed
in as the interactive user, and it spends that user's own allowance, so nothing happens until
you switch it on in Settings.
readPdf   - also hand over the offline copy when there is one. This is what lets a summary say
anything about baseline tables and figures, which is where unreported confounding
usually hides. With no offline copy it falls back to the abstract alone.
maxPerRun - how many papers one run of the scheduled task will do. Small on purpose, because
each one spends your own subscription allowance.
_trial_comment: Signals that a paper is an interventional trial. PubMed's 'Randomized Controlled Trial[pt]' filter
CANNOT be used for this: it only matches MEDLINE-indexed records, and brand-new papers are
'Publisher'/'In-Process' status for weeks. Verified 2026-10-03. So trials are detected from the
text and from registry identifiers instead, which work from day one.
